newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson sees big potential from new mobile phone.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson sees big potential from new mobile phone.

text.p: Developing a new third generation mobile telephone with Wideband Code Division Multiple Access (W-CDMA) technology promises Ericsson a new growth market, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
"The potential is really big ... we are now seeing a change-over from NMT in Europe to GSM," said Hans Jarne of Ericsson Radio Systems.
"But then this will be taken over by a third generation mobile telephony."

The broadband W-CDMA techology is an advanced digital wireless technology that increases data transfer rates to two Mbps for short distances and to 384 kbps for long distances, Ericsson spokesman Per Bengtsson said.
This compares to GSM technology that can handle 64 Kbps.
The new system can therefore offer more multi-media services including full motion video, video conferencing and Internet access.
Ericsson said earlier on Thursday that it was jointly developing an experimental third generation wireless system for Japan's NTT DoCoMo.
Ericsson did not want to reveal how much NTT DoCoMo will pay for the task and would not diclose either how big an investment it would mean for Ericsson in terms of development costs.
NTT DoCoMo said it was to invest aobut 60 billion yen in the system.
Bengtsson said Japan is Ericsson's third largest market for mobile systems after the U.S. and China. The Japanese market has one of the highest growth rates.
"Japan is the fastest growing market," said Bengtsson.
Currently there is about 20 million mobile phone subscribers in Japan, according to Bengtsson.
But it is estimated that this number could rise to 45 million by the year 2000.
The first commercial systrem with W-CDMA technology is not expected to come onto the mearket until the start of 2000.
"During 1998 it will be tested indoors and these tests will continue outdoors in 1999," Bengtsson said.
